input.question: How allergy shots work.
input.ground_truth: They inject you with a *really tiny* amount of the allergen at first, then subsequent shots up the dosage a little bit at a time. It exposes your body to the allergen in such a way that it never freaks out and eventually realizes that there isn't actually a threat.

Question: How allergy shots work.

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a tiny friend who doesn’t like cats, and every time they see a cat, they start sneezing and get itchy because they are allergic to cats. 

Allergy shots are like giving your body a tiny, tiny bit of the thing it doesn’t like (like a little bit of cat stuff), but in a safe way. 

At first, your body says, “Oh no! Cat stuff!” and gets a little upset. But after you get the shot many times, your body starts to learn, “Hey, this isn’t so bad. I can handle this!” 

So, after a while, your body doesn’t get so upset when it sees the real thing. That’s how allergy shots help you not get as sick or itchy when you’re around what you’re allergic to. 

It’s like teaching your body to be friends with the cat instead of being scared!
